raw_response:
My land is about 9 mu of flat ground. I've been farming here since I was a teenager helping my father. This land is good for wheat and corn — that's what my neighbors grow, that's what the grain station buys, and that's what I know how to do well. I won't try cotton anymore; prices have been bad for years and it needs too much hand labor.

I'll put 8 mu into the winter wheat–summer maize rotation I've always done. Plant the wheat in October after the fall rains, harvest in early June, then immediately push the corn into the stubble. The other mu I keep as a vegetable plot near the house — garlic, cabbage, some chili. Mostly for my family; sell a little to neighbors.

For wheat I'll use Jimai 22 again — the seed store always has it, yield is reliable, and I know how it behaves in my soil. I'll plough and apply compound base fertilizer before sowing, then top-dress urea when it greens up in March. Three irrigations: before winter freeze, at green-up, and at heading. Two sprays — herbicide right after germination, and something for aphids in May.

For the corn I won't till — just direct-seed Xianyu 335 hybrid into the wheat stubble with the seeder. Apply fertilizer at planting and again at big bell stage. Summer rains usually cover water needs but I'll irrigate once at tasseling if it's dry. Watch for fall armyworm; I'll spray once as prevention and once if I actually see damage.
